paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole song is about: being near God is the best thing there is. The singer doesn't just say it's nice. He says his soul "longs, even faints," and that his "heart and my flesh cry out for the living God" (Psalm 84:2). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, I know what it is to ache for a better place. But this man isn't aching for a place. He's aching for GOD.

Now look at how he gets there. He calls blessed the people whose "strength is in You," the ones whose "hearts are set on pilgrimage" (Psalm 84:5). Even a dry valley like Baca turns into "a place of springs" when they pass through (Psalm 84:6). They go "from strength to strength, until each appears before God in Zion" (Psalm 84:7). The hard stretches of your road don't have to be where you quit. God can meet you right in the middle of them.

So what do you do with that, baker? You trust Him, and you choose Him like the singer did: "better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere" (Psalm 84:10). Why? Because "the LORD God is a sun and a shield; the LORD gives grace and glory; He withholds no good thing from those who walk with integrity" (Psalm 84:11). The song ends where it should: "O LORD of Hosts, how blessed is the man who trusts in You!" (Psalm 84:12). Keep your heart set on the road, friend, and keep walking.
